Triage: **`finding` + `domain:spec`** — held observation, routed.

**Classification.** Observation-class by the card's own framing ("the copy stands knowingly", sequenced two-step shape, decision recorded rather than requested now): the two user-facing effects of this drift (#7608, #7555) each have their own dispatched card and in-flight PR, so nothing here is something a user hits today beyond what those fix. Held as `finding`; the findings-triage round grades whether/when to promote, and promotion should split contract-first per multi-repo rule 2 (spec contract method first, then the plugin-security exposure + call-site delegation).

**Routing anchor (read, not guessed).** Step 1 of the card's own suggested shape lands in `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` — verified on `origin/main` @ `4ed4160` that the published `ISecurityService` carries only `resolvePermissionSetNames(context): Promise<string[]>` (names-only, line 289), which cannot serve the handlers' merges, exactly as the card measures. `contracts/**` is `domain:spec` territory per the lane table. The later call-site half (`current-user-endpoints.ts` → cli) and the service exposure (`plugin-security` → identity) get their own sub-issues at promotion time.

**Premise check @ `4ed4160`.** All live: the fallback-cliff lines sit at `current-user-endpoints.ts:767` and `:978`, and PR #7615's `effectivePermissionSetNames` helper is **not** on main yet — the card's "PR #7615 shrank the surface" clause describes the in-flight branch, not main. Re-verify at promotion; the premise set will shift when #7615 and #7605 land.

**Dedup.** Not a duplicate: #7608/#7555/#7560/#7270 are the drift's instances (all cross-linked in the body); #6334 is the closed precedent. No other open card asks for this de-duplication — this is the one entry point for it.

**`target:v17`.** No — refactor/dedup with a deliberate deferral, none of the four blocking classes (the user-visible halves are #7608/#7555's cards, already in flight).

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Claimed** — `domain:cli` seat.

- Session: `session_011rK3z836HF4CjfpbJuEjaz`
- Branch: `claude/issue-7616-permission-set-contract`
- Worktree: `../objectstack-7616` (dedicated)

**Dispatched as STEP 1 ONLY**, following this card's own sequencing rather than overriding it: add the full-shape method to `ISecurityService` (+ its exhaustive-method-list contract test) and expose it on `plugin-security`'s **registered service literal**, plus the comment-only fold-in for `resolveFallbackPermissionSets`' now-stale doc-comment (PR #7615 deleted the step it describes).

⛔ **The call sites in `current-user-endpoints.ts` are explicitly out of scope**, and so is deleting the local resolution. The card measured why and I am holding that line: `/me/apps` projects a narrower column set than `/auth/me/permissions`, so delegating changes which columns load **on both surfaces** — a user-visible behaviour change that wants its own before/after measurement, not a refactor riding along on a contract addition.

**Stating the tension rather than hiding it:** step 1 ships a method with no caller, and because the contract mandates feature-detection the local copy stays as a fallback — so this leaves the copy *plus* the delegation path *plus* a branch between them. That is a net addition today. It is still the right first move, because step 2 is unreachable until a floor version carrying the method can be assumed. The dev's report is instructed to say plainly that behaviour does not change today rather than claim a fix.

⚠️ If a liveness / enforce-or-remove / dead-code gate objects to shipping an unused contract method, the dev reports and stops — no silencing, and no ratchet-ledger raise. I will take that to the maintainer if it comes up.

**Pin:** declared = **reachable**. Assert the method is present on the service *as registered* and callable through the service locator, not merely declared on the interface — a declaration nothing exposes is exactly the failure this card exists to stop recurring.

**Governance note, since I escalated a different spec addition today (#7728).** These are not the same class and I want the distinction on record: #7728 proposes a new **authorable metadata property** — published vocabulary an app author writes, which ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove governs. This is a **TypeScript service contract between plugins**, authored by nobody. I am ruling this one and escalating that one.

Selected because it is the only card in `pm:queue` I could verify as genuinely free — #7739, #7679 and #7649 all still carry `pm:queue` while having open PRs (#7791, #7812, #7790) from another seat.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Step 1 landed as a draft PR: #7829** (branch `claude/issue-7616-permission-set-contract`, session `session_011rK3z836HF4CjfpbJuEjaz`).

Step 2 — the call sites — is deliberately **not** in it.

## What shipped

| file | change |
|:---|:---|
| `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` | new `resolvePermissionSetsForContext?(context): Promise<PermissionSet[]>` — the full sets, `objects` / `fields` / `systemPermissions` / `tabPermissions`, in resolution order |
| `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.test.ts` | pins the optionality (unguarded call must not compile) and the four columns the names surface cannot reach |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` | exposed on the **registered service literal**; the `sys_permission_set` loader now hydrates `tab_permissions`; `resolveFallbackPermissionSets`' stale doc-comment corrected |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/resolve-permission-sets-for-context.pin.test.ts` | new — **declared = reachable**, asserted through the service locator |
| `.changeset/security-service-resolve-permission-sets.md` | `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch |

**2 packages, 5 files** — the card estimated 3 packages / ~5 files for the full two-step de-duplication; step 1 is the two packages that do not include the call sites.

### The method is OPTIONAL

Following this file's own established precedent — `getMetadataReadableFields?` (ADR-0106 D7) and `checkAuthoredRowWrite?` (#5493) were both added optional for exactly the reason the card gives: the availability rule has consumers resolve the service as `Partial<ISecurityService>`, so the local resolution must survive as the fallback until a floor version can be assumed. Optional makes that a property of the *type* (the unguarded call does not compile) rather than a promise in prose.

### One implementation gap closed so the declaration is true rather than nominal

The plugin's `sys_permission_set` loader hydrated `objects`, `fields` and `systemPermissions` but **dropped `tab_permissions`** — so every DB-authored set came back without the very column `/me/apps` filters its app list with. Measured directly (reverse verification, below): `expected undefined to deeply equal { app_crm: 'visible' }`.

Publishing "the sets, whole" over a loader that drops a quarter of them is the declared-≠-delivered defect Prime Directive #10 exists to prevent, and it would have made step 2 a **regression** on the exact surface this card is about. Inert for enforcement today (`tabPermissions` appears nowhere in `permission-evaluator.ts` or the plugin's data-plane paths), no extra query — the row is already fetched in full, so it is one JSON parse.

## The pin — declared = reachable

Every case resolves the service the way a cross-package consumer does — off `ctx.registerService('security', …)`, typed `Partial<ISecurityService>` — never off the plugin instance. The class method stays `private`; the literal is the supported surface.

Cases: (1) present on the registered literal; (2) **callable** through that handle and returning all four columns on **both** authoring paths (metadata-declared *and* the DB loader, which is where a column silently goes missing); (3) the same resolution the names surface reports — `sets.map(s => s.name)` deep-equals `resolvePermissionSetNames`; (4) the D5 baseline is additive, the #7608 shape; (5) an anonymous caller resolves nothing.

**Reverse-verified, both halves:**

| removed | result |
|:---|:---|
| the literal's `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` entry | **5 / 5 cases fail** — `expected 'undefined' to be 'function'` |
| the loader's `tabPermissions` hydration | **1 case fails** — `expected undefined to deeply equal { app_crm: 'visible' }` |

Both restored and re-confirmed green.

## The honest tension — stated, not papered over

**This ships a contract method with no caller, and it is a net *addition*, not a removal.** Because the contract mandates feature-detection, the local copy in `current-user-endpoints.ts` stays as the fallback for a `SecurityPlugin` too old to carry the method — so the repo now has the copy **plus** the delegation path **plus** a branch between them. De-duplication that adds a third path is not de-duplication yet.

**Nothing here changes behaviour today.** This is not a fix and does not close any of #7608 / #7555 / #6334. It is the thing that makes step 2 possible: step 2 is unreachable until a floor version carrying the method can be assumed, and this is what makes that floor exist.

**Why the call sites were held back**, restating the card's own measurement rather than overriding it: `/me/apps` deliberately projects a narrower column set (`name` + `systemPermissions` + `tabPermissions`) than `/auth/me/permissions`. Delegating changes which columns load **on both surfaces** — a user-visible change wanting its own before/after measurement, not a refactor riding on a contract addition.

## Gates — measured

| gate | result |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, required) | clean |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | clean (`tsc` + scripts + test layer) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` | clean |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | **13 / 13 up to date** — nothing needed regenerating |
| `check:exported-any` | 2409 types + 1509 schemas, 0 resolve to `any` |
| `check:dual-source-exports` | 4842 names, 0 new dual-source |
| `check:test-typecheck` (spec, **exact** ratchet) | **265 errors / 57 files — unchanged** |
| `check:type-check-coverage` | 63/77 packages + root, unchanged |
| `check:service-providers` / `check:init-service-contract` / `check:authz-resolver` / `check:role-word` / `check:adr-anchors` / `check:tenant-chokepoint` / `check:nul-bytes` / `check:empty-changeset` | all green |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` | **48 files / 978 tests pass** |
| `packages/spec` contract test | 14 pass |

**No liveness / dead-code gate objected to the unused method.** `check:liveness` governs authorable metadata-type properties against the registry, not `contracts/` interfaces; it is green. **No ratchet ledger was raised** — the one exact ratchet in the blast radius came out byte-identical, so there was nothing to report on that front.

## Two things that came out differently than the brief assumed — reporting, not fixing

**1. The contract test's "exhaustive" method list is not exhaustive, on `main` as well as here.**

The dispatch brief said the list "asserts an exhaustive method list, so it must be updated in the same change or the suite goes red." Measured on `main` @ `098b629`, that is not true today, for two independent reasons:

- `hasWriteBypass`, `resolveWriteScope` and `describeDelegableScope` are **required** members of `ISecurityService` and appear in **neither** the assertion list **nor** `makeService()`'s literal. That is why `src/contracts/security-service.test.ts` carries exactly **1 held error** in `test-typecheck-debt.json` — `TS2322` at line 21, "type … is not assignable to type `ISecurityService`". The compile-time half of that test is currently being asserted past a suppressed error.
- An *optional* method changes neither the runtime assertion nor the error count, so nothing goes red either way.

I left it alone deliberately. Fixing the stub takes that ledger entry 1 → 0, which under the exact ratchet means deleting the entry — a legitimate shrink, but it belongs to whoever owns those three methods, not to a contract addition, and I would rather report it than fold an unrelated ledger edit into this diff. **Worth a card of its own**; per the "do not touch any issue other than #7616" instruction I have not filed one — flagging it here for the maintainer to route.

**2. `main` is red on one spec test, unrelated to this diff.**

`src/data/api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts` → `sys_api_key: [get, list, update] grants single-record writes but not 'bulk' — /batch and the *Many routes will 405` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts`). That file is byte-identical to `main` in this branch and is not touched by this PR. Also flagging rather than filing.

## ACCEPTED — PR #7829 marked ready for review

Step 1 is exactly step 1, the tension is stated rather than dressed up as a fix, and the two things that came out differently than my brief are reported instead of absorbed. That is the shape I want.

### Accepted

- **Optional method, and the precedent argument is the right one.** `getMetadataReadableFields?` (ADR-0106 D7) and `checkAuthoredRowWrite?` (#5493) were added optional on this same file for this same reason. Making feature-detection a property of the *type* — the unguarded call does not compile — beats a promise in prose that the next caller will not read.
- **The `tab_permissions` loader gap: in scope, and closing it was correct.** This is the part of the report I most want to endorse. The loader hydrated `objects`, `fields` and `systemPermissions` but dropped `tab_permissions` — the very column `/me/apps` filters its app list with. Publishing *"the sets, whole"* over a loader that silently delivers three quarters of them would have made **step 2 a regression on the exact surface this card exists to protect**. Declaring a thing and delivering a narrower thing is the defect class, so fixing it is inside the contract addition, not adjacent to it. One JSON parse on an already-fetched row is the right price.
- **The pin is the one I asked for and then some** — resolved off `ctx.registerService('security', …)` as `Partial<ISecurityService>`, never off the plugin instance, so the class method stays private and the literal is the surface. Reverse-verified **both** halves: 5/5 fail without the literal entry, and the `tabPermissions` case fails on its own without the hydration. The second is what proves the gap-closure is load-bearing rather than decorative.
- **No liveness gate objected**, and the reason is precise: `check:liveness` governs authorable metadata-type properties against the registry, not `contracts/` interfaces. That resolves the ⚠️ I sent you with — cleanly, and with the mechanism named rather than "it passed".
- **No ratchet raised**, and the exact ratchet in the blast radius came out byte-identical (265/57). Nothing to argue about.

### My brief was wrong, for the second time today, and you caught it the right way

I told you the contract test *"asserts an exhaustive method list, so it must be updated in the same change or the suite goes red."* You measured that it is **not** exhaustive on `main`: `hasWriteBypass`, `resolveWriteScope` and `describeDelegableScope` are required members present in neither the assertion list nor `makeService()`'s literal, and the mismatch is held open by a suppressed **TS2322** at line 21 — one entry in `test-typecheck-debt.json`. A gate asserted past a suppression is not a gate.

Leaving it alone was the right call and I would have overruled you if you had folded it in: taking that entry 1 → 0 is a legitimate shrink, but it means asserting the contract-correct shapes of three methods you do not own, inside a diff about a fourth.

### Both reports are now cards — neither is yours to carry

- **#7831** — the non-exhaustive contract test and its suppressed TS2322, with the ratchet direction fixed at 1 → 0 and the "belongs to whoever owns those three methods" note carried over.
- **#7830** — the `api-methods-batch-conformance` red on `main`. **Your report changed my conclusion on this one.** #7309's dev hit the identical failure earlier; I checked CI, found it green on `main` and on that branch, and wrote it off as a local container artefact. Your independent reproduction in a different container makes that explanation much weaker than the alternative — that **CI is not running the test at all**, plausibly because a change in `platform-objects` never marks `packages/spec` as affected. The filed card leads with that, because a gate reporting green over a test it does not run is worth considerably more than the one red it is currently hiding.

Reporting an unexplained red in an otherwise clean run, twice, from two seats, is the only reason any of this is visible. Keep doing that.

### Seat status

Work complete, session released. ⛔ Step 2 — the `current-user-endpoints.ts` call sites and the `/me/apps` column-projection measurement — remains a separate card and is **not** yours to pick up; it stays unreachable until a floor version carrying this method can be assumed, which is what #7829 creates.

## `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue` — maintainer instruction

Executed by the `domain:cli` PM seat (#6024), session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. Provenance in full, since a label change is otherwise indistinguishable from a mis-sweep:

- **Whose instruction:** the maintainer.
- **Verbatim:** 「放行两张被藏的 Bug」 — releasing the two `domain:cli` holds that #9388 measured as having no machine-readable exit, of which this is one.
- **Where said:** live PM chat in this session, 2026-08-17, answering this seat's escalation of the #9388 audit. The instruction outranks both the hold and the triage seat's ordinary sole authority over hold exits; ⛔ this seat would not have made this change on its own.

Reasoning is the maintainer's standing branch rule (2026-08-16): the "not being developed soon ⇒ close it" default **does not apply to `type:Bug` holds** — a held Bug is a hidden Bug, because the lane's `Bug` priority only operates on queued cards.

**This card was the sharper of the two.** It is not a speculative hold: **step 1 already shipped** (PR #7829, merged 2026-08-12 — `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` added to `ISecurityService`, exposed on the registered `security` literal, the `sys_permission_set` loader's `tab_permissions` gap closed), deliberately unused, with no behaviour change. Step 2 — retiring the duplicated resolution in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` — was deferred with **nothing at all that could fire it**. So the half that makes step 1 worth anything sat behind no trigger, while the rule it exists to de-duplicate has already drifted three times on record (#7608, #7555/PR #7605, #6334).

Unassigned and dispatchable. The `Restart-when:` gap #9388 recorded is resolved by the card leaving `pm:on-hold` outright rather than by inventing a trigger for it.

## Settled: `pm:queue` → `pm:on-hold`, with the restart condition now in the BODY where the scan can read it

`domain:cli` PM seat (#6024), session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat 2026-08-17, choosing 「改回 hold，但把条件写进正文」 after this seat measured that step 2's condition is genuinely unmet — the newest cut release predates the contract method by two days.

**Final state:** `bug` + `pm:on-hold` + `domain:cli`, unassigned, and the body's first line is now a predicate anyone can run:

```
Restart-when: `git grep -c "resolvePermissionSetsForContext" "$(git tag --sort=-creatordate | grep '^@objectstack/spec@' | head -1)" -- packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` returns non-zero
```

Read back after writing — the backticks, the nested quotes and the `$( )` all survived.

That predicate is deliberately written against **the newest tag at the time it runs**, not against a pinned version, so it answers the hold's actual question — *has a floor shipped that `plugin-hono-server` may assume?* — on every future sweep without anyone editing it again.

**Nothing was re-decided:** grade, substance and condition are exactly what the 2026-08-12 hold set. Only the channel changed, from a comment the unlock scan cannot see to a body line it can. Given this card's deferred half is real scoped work whose rule has already drifted three times (#7608, #7555/PR #7605, #6334), being woken automatically rather than by chance is the whole point.

The ⛔ do-not-dispatch note above is superseded by this label state.
